title: Falls and Accident Prevention
subtitle: For staff at Pennsylvania personal care homes and assisted living facilities. 55 Pa. Code 2600.65(g)(5) and 2800.65(j)(5).

title: Who is at risk, and why it changes week to week

eyebrow: Highest risk right after a change
title: Medications that put residents on the floor
points: Anything newly started, stopped, or adjusted

title: The change that arrives before the fall
points: New confusion, new unsteadiness, new sleepiness

title: What sets a resident's baseline risk
points: A previous fall — the strongest single predictor
Blood pressure that drops on standing
Dementia, and the depth perception it takes

title: The fifteen seconds before you leave the room
Check these before you walk out
points: Walker or cane where they can get it
Path clear enough to walk in the dark

eyebrow: Look at the room like you have never seen it
title: What you are looking for
points: Clutter or a cord across the path
The bathroom light that has been out a week
Bed too high for their feet to reach

eyebrow: What a slow call bell teaches
quote: A bell answered quickly teaches a resident that waiting is safe.
attribution: A bell nobody answers teaches them to handle it themselves. That lesson gets taught on day shift and cashed in at three in the morning.

title: Transfers, and where good people get hurt
Slow it down and set it up
points: Tell them what is about to happen
Sit on the edge of the bed before standing
Keep them close, use your legs, never lift under the arms

quote: Never attempt a technique or a piece of equipment you have not been checked off on for that resident.
attribution: Nobody has ever been written up for asking for a second set of hands. Plenty of people have been hurt doing it alone.

title: The minutes after you find somebody on the floor
Do not move a resident who has
points: Hit their head, or might have
Pain in the neck, back, or hip

quote: A resident telling you they did not hit their head is not the same as knowing they did not.
attribution: They were confused enough to end up on the floor. Treat it as a head injury until somebody qualified says otherwise.

eyebrow: What you saw, not your theory about it
title: Write down
points: Where they were and in what position
What they said, in their words
What you found when you looked
The wet floor, the broken brake, the light that was out

eyebrow: What to carry out of this course
quote: The goal was never no movement. It is safe movement.
attribution: A resident who never moves gets weaker, and weaker is what causes the next fall.

quote: Fear of falling is its own injury.
attribution: Nothing broke. Nothing showed up on an x-ray. And a resident who walked to activities every afternoon now asks for a wheelchair to cross a hallway.

title: Get a second set of hands when
points: You have not been checked off on that equipment
The resident is heavier or weaker than you expected
Anything about the setup has changed
